message.content:
**Typical time‑difference**

| City | Standard time | Daylight‑saving time |
|------|---------------|---------------------|
| **Los Angeles** | Pacific Standard Time (PST) –08:00 UTC | Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) –07:00 UTC |
| **Berlin**      | Central European Time (CET)   +01:00 UTC | Central European Summer Time (CEST)+02:00 UTC |

Because both regions move forward together once per year, the *usual* gap stays constant:

```
Berlin → Los Angeles : −9 hours
(so Berlin is always 9 h ahead)
```

So, e.g.:

* If it’s **12:00 pm noon** in Berlin, it will be **03:00 am** the same day in Los Angeles.
* Conversely, if it’s **09:00 am** in Los Angeles, it’ll be **18:00 or 6:00 p.m.** in Berlin.

---

### When does this differ?

Both places switch to/from daylight savings on slightly different dates:

| Transition | Los Angeles (US/Canada) | Berlin (Germany/EU) |
|------------|------------------------|--------------------|
| Start DST | Second Sunday in March | Last Sunday in March |
| End DST   | First Sunday in November | Last Sunday in October |

During those few weeks when only one side has switched, the gap temporarily becomes either **8 hours** or **10 hours**:

| Period | Gap |
|--------|-----|
| Early March (before US starts DST, after EU already started) | 10 hrs (LA behind by 10 hrs) |
| Late September / early October (after US ends DST, before EU ends) | 8 hrs (LA behind by 8 hrs) |

After both sides finish switching back, the normal 9‑hour difference resumes until the next cycle.

---

#### Quick reference table (current season)

| Date range (typical 2025–26) | LA time zone | Berlin time zone | Δ (Berlin minus LA) |
|------------------------------|-------------|------------------|-------------------|
| Mid‑March to end‑October     | PDT (−7)    | CEST (+2)        | 9 hr              |
| Early Nov to mid‑Mar         | PST (−8)    | CET (+1)         | 9 hr              |
| Early Mar (first week)       | PST          | CEST             | 10 hr             |
| Late Oct (last week)         | PDT          | CET               | 8 hr              |

*(Exact dates vary yearly; see official government calendars.)*

---

If you ever need the exact current offset right now, just let me know your preferred format (e.g., “what's the time in Berlin when it's 14:30 in L.A.”) and I can do the calculation instantly!
